validation_strategy:
**Per-phase validation.** Each phase runs the focused suites for the surfaces it touched, then one full scenario suite. Focused commands: 'cd scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/api && go test -count=1 ./...' for api, the same in cli/ and runtime/, and 'cd scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/ui && pnpm test:coverage' for ui. Gate commands after Phase 12: 'make lint' and 'make fmt' from the scenario root, both of which must exercise every Go module and the TypeScript surface.

**Full suite protocol.** Run 'vrooli scenario test scenario-to-desktop'. The run is server-owned and survives a cancelled shell. Block exactly once with 'test-genie runs wait --json --timeout=3600 scenario-to-desktop <run-id>'. Never poll. Read the scorecard with 'test-genie runs findings <run-id> --scenario scenario-to-desktop'. Only Test Genie terminal evidence establishes a verdict.

**Evidence that counts.** A phase is proven by a fresh full run, not a cached one. Test Genie tagged the anchor run evidence_tier=degraded with five phases (business, docs, proto, structure, unit) on stale evidence. A phase acceptance that rests on a stale phase is not met. Check the staleEvidence list in the completeness block and re-run if the phase you changed appears there.

**Determinism evidence is different in kind.** Phase 1 cannot prove determinism with a single green run, because the anchor state is a suite that sometimes passes. It requires 20 consecutive clean runs of each suite, recorded, with zero flips. Later phases inherit that guarantee and need only a single clean run each.

**Proto migration validation is contract-level, not just test-level.** Phases 5 through 8 must each show proto-health advancing, checked through the proto phase of the full suite. Phase 5 clears package_mismatch, shared_type_misplaced, and unsupported_annotation. Phases 6 and 8 clear proto_adoption_missing for the api and cli surfaces respectively. Phase 8 clears possibly_unused by making all 25 orphaned messages reachable from a served RPC or deleting them. Generated code must be regenerated through the repository's buf pipeline, never hand-edited. Skip buf breaking-change checks on this feature branch, per standing repository practice.

**Behavioral validation for the migration.** Test parity, not just compilation. Before Phase 6 deletes or replaces anything, record the response body of each REST route that has a Connect replacement. After the cutover, assert the Connect response carries the same information. The three packages with hand-rolled envelopes (captures, deploy, livedesktop) currently emit a bare error object; Phase 9 must show them emitting the same rich envelope as the other 13, verified by an assertion on the error shape rather than by inspection.

**Security validation.** Phase 10 is proven when the security phase reports zero unexplained errors. Every remaining suppression must carry a justification at the site. Verify the VNC binding change by observing that x11vnc and websockify listen only on the loopback interface during an active live-desktop session, not by reading the source.

**Final validation.** A reviewer runs, from the repository root:
1. 'vrooli scenario start scenario-to-desktop' and confirms healthy status.
2. 'vrooli scenario test scenario-to-desktop', then the single wait command above.
3. 'test-genie runs findings <run-id> --scenario scenario-to-desktop' and confirms verdict PASS, completeness at or above 85, evidence_tier not degraded, and no phase at L0.
4. 'make lint' and 'make fmt' from scenarios/scenario-to-desktop and confirms both exercise api, cli, runtime, and ui.
5. A baseline diff against the Phase 0 anchor showing no metric regressed.

title: Portal v0 core: scaffold, chat transplant, readiness registry, passive search
purpose: Portal is the chat-first front door to the Vrooli ecosystem — the operator-approved greenfield successor to agent-inbox and app-monitor (initiative portal-front-door, 2026-07-03). This plan delivers v0, the foundation everything else builds on: the scaffolded `portal` scenario with a working chat core transplanted from agent-inbox, an integration readiness registry that keeps the product honest and usable while dependencies degrade, and the PASSIVE search loop that lets the ecosystem surface its own capabilities in conversation without ever gating the LLM. Two follow-up plans extend it: scenario embeds + feedback loop (plan 2), and the FULL short-circuit gate, widgets, and voice (plan 3).
scope: In scope: the new `portal` scenario end to end (api/, ui/, cli/, docs/, .vrooli/, test suite); new packages/proto/schemas/portal/v1 contracts + generated code; chat core (OpenRouter LLM chat, agent mode via agent-manager, message tree, skills-to-system-prompt, usage capture); integration readiness registry + mode ladder + settings override + mode indicator; PASSIVE search loop (omnibox suggestions, async result attachment, next-turn context injection, basic typed hit cards); sidebar with grouped chats; PWA/mobile-first basics; i18n wiring (en content, fleet-standard toolchain). Out of scope (later plans/items): scenario embeds in chat and the screenshot/logs/network feedback loop (plan 2); the FULL short-circuit gate, answer cards with auto-display, retrieval eval harness, widget runtime, voice input (plan 3); any search-hub changes (backlog item execute/search-hub-interactive-readiness); deleting agent-inbox/app-monitor (chore/portal-retire-agent-inbox-app-monitor); chat-history migration (start clean); any web-console changes (separate monetized product).

title: P5 — Interactive Run Bridge + Computer-Use Agent extraction
purpose:
Give agent-manager a first-class **interactive run** mode and turn BAS's browser-only "vision agent" loop into a **reusable, surface-agnostic computer-use package**.

Today agent-manager only runs **headless coding agents** (claude-code / codex / opencode) as host or sandbox OS processes; their entire lifecycle is `stdin prompt → stdout transcript → exit`. There is no way for agent-manager to *drive an interactive TTY* (answer a prompt, press a key, observe a screen) under its run authority. Separately, BAS already has a complete observe→decide→act loop with vision-model clients, action vocabulary, and loop detection — but it is welded to Playwright/the browser and locked inside one scenario, so no other surface can reuse it.

P5 unifies both: agent-manager grows an **interactive Run** launched via a new `WebConsoleLauncher` (web-console session as the TTY substrate), and the observe→decide→act loop becomes `packages/computer-use-agent`, a TypeScript enabler package with a generic surface-adapter seam. BAS becomes the **browser** adapter; agent-manager + web-console become the **terminal** adapter. The terminal adapter is wired as the **decision-answerer** for interactive runs, gated by P4's state classifier + permission matrix so risky prompts escalate to a human instead of being auto-answered.

---
non_goals:
- **No compatibility layer / dead code / re-exports / `_unused` shims.** The in-BAS loop is deleted in the phase that lands its replacement (§0).
- **No second loop.** There is exactly one observe→decide→act loop, in `packages/computer-use-agent`. No Go re-port, no BAS-private copy.
- **No parallel Session lifecycle.** agent-manager's Run is the sole authority; the web-console Session is referenced by id (a launcher detail). No web-console→agent-manager ownership callback.
- **No auto-answering risky prompts.** Destructive/irreversible/unknown states escalate to a human via the existing approval workflow — fail-closed.
- **No raw package managers.** All deps via SDA (Critical Rule §5).
- **No hand-edited `.vrooli/endpoints.json`** and **no new REST exception** for interactive runs — Connect-RPC only.
- **No `make breaking` mid-development**; the tree builds at every phase boundary.
- **Do not build P1/P2/P3/P4 contracts here** — consume them.

---

- [ ] `packages/computer-use-agent` exists, builds (ESM + CJS), is fully unit-tested, and has **zero** Playwright/browser imports — a surface-agnostic enabler package.
- [ ] BAS imports the package and is a thin **browser adapter**; the in-BAS loop is deleted; BAS vision-navigate behavior is unchanged (parity tests + baseline diff exit 0).
- [ ] agent-manager runs an **interactive Run** (`kind=coding-agent, exec_mode=interactive`) via `WebConsoleLauncher`, with one-directional Run↔Session mapping and recovery (adopt-not-kill); the run is listable, drainable (`QuiesceScenario`), stoppable, and recoverable.
- [ ] A **terminal surface adapter** consumes the package: configurable observe mode (text default / screenshot only for vision models), act via `SendInput`, paced by `WaitIdle`.
- [ ] The computer-use agent is the **decision-answerer**, governed by P4's permission matrix: `auto_proceed` → answer; `pause_for_human`/`escalate_to_approval`/unknown/destructive → `needs_review` + existing approval workflow. problem_statement:
**Problem A — agent-manager cannot run interactive agents.** Every agent-manager run is headless: the `Launcher` seam launches an OS process whose contract is `stdin → stdout transcript → exit` (`launcher.go:51` `Launch`, `:87` `LaunchedProcess`). There is no Run that *attaches to a live TTY*, answers a prompt, presses a key, or reads a rendered screen. Use cases that need a human-or-agent at a keyboard (interactive installers, REPLs, agents that pause for an approval prompt, "drive this CLI to completion") have no home under agent-manager's run authority. web-console already provides a perfect TTY substrate (programmatic `SendInput`/`GetScreen`/`WaitIdle` + tmux-backed session recovery) but nothing wires it under a Run.

**Problem B — the computer-use loop is trapped in BAS.** BAS's `playwright-driver/src/ai/vision-agent/agent.ts` is a complete, production observe→decide→act loop (loop `agent.ts:114`, observe `:265`/`:692`, decide `:374`, act `:514`, loop-detect `:554`, emit `:616`) with vision clients (Claude Computer Use + OpenRouter), a 10-verb action vocabulary, and a dedicated loop detector (`loop-detection.ts`). It is welded to Playwright: `NavigationConfig.page: Page` (`types.ts:22`), and three of the six `VisionAgentDeps` (`types.ts:150`) — `screenshotCapture`, `annotator`, `actionExecutor` — are browser-specific. The loop *itself* (decide via vision client, detect loops, emit steps) is surface-agnostic but cannot be reused by any non-browser surface. There is **no shared TypeScript package** under `packages/` today (all current packages are Go except `@vrooli/iframe-bridge`, `@vrooli/api-base`, `@vrooli/vitest-requirement-reporter`).

**Problem C — interactive autonomy has no governor.** If an agent drives a terminal, "should the agent answer this prompt itself, or stop for a human?" must be governed. P4 builds the answer (`ServiceDescriptor.state_detectors[]` + `permission_matrix{state → auto_proceed | pause_for_human | escalate_to_approval}`). P5 must *consume* that gate so destructive/irreversible prompts escalate to agent-manager's existing approval workflow, never auto-answered.

**Cross-plan dependencies (verified absent today — they are P1/P4 deliverables, not P5's):**
- `ServiceDescriptor`, `permission_matrix`, `auto_proceed`/`pause_for_human`/`escalate_to_approval` — `grep` over `scenarios/agent-manager` + `packages/proto/schemas` returns **zero** product hits (only third-party `descriptor_pb` noise). **Built by P4.** P5 imports them.
- `UsageEvent` / usage spine — **zero** hits in `scenarios/agent-manager/api` + `packages/proto/schemas/agent-manager`. **Built by P1.** P5 emits into it.
- The resolver / Policy (P2/P3) — P5 may resolve a `vision-navigate` Intent through it but does not build it.

**Execution ordering consequence:** P5 must be authored against the P4/P1 contract *shapes* (see §8), and its phases gate on those contracts being mergeable. The terminal-adapter autonomy gate (Phase 5) and the UsageEvent emission (Phase 3) are the only places P5 hard-couples to P4/P1; structure them behind a thin interface so P5's earlier phases land even if P4/P1 are mid-flight (see §11 R-7).

---
target_outcome:
1. **agent-manager runs interactive agents.** A Run created with `kind=coding-agent, mode=interactive` resolves to the `WebConsoleLauncher`, which creates a web-console session, drives it, and treats the session as a launcher detail (a "PID"). The Run is the single authority; on web-console crash, agent-manager owns recovery by reusing web-console's `Recover` (adopt-not-kill). Interactive runs appear in `ListRuns`, are drainable by `QuiesceScenario`, can be `StopRun`-ned, and emit `UsageEvent{kind=agent_run}` into P1's spine.
2. **`packages/computer-use-agent` exists** as a published-shape, surface-agnostic TypeScript enabler package: the observe→decide→act loop, vision clients (Claude Computer Use + OpenRouter), action vocabulary, loop detector, and step-emitter, behind a clean `ObserveService` / `ActionExecutor` / surface-adapter seam (generalized `VisionAgentDeps`). It has zero Playwright / browser imports.
3. **BAS is a thin browser adapter over the package.** `playwright-driver` imports `@vrooli/computer-use-agent`; its `screenshot`/`annotate`/`executor` implement the package's `ObserveService`/`ActionExecutor` interfaces. The old in-BAS loop copy is **deleted**. `session-ai-navigate.ts` wires package + browser adapter. BAS behavior is unchanged (same vision navigate result).
4. **agent-manager has a terminal surface adapter** consuming the package: `observe` = web-console `GetScreen` (configurable: `plain_text` for cheap/non-vision models, screenshot for vision models); `act` = `SendInput` (keys/text, source-attributed); pacing via `WaitIdle`.
5. **Autonomy is governed.** The computer-use agent is the decision-answerer for interactive runs, gated by P4's `permission_matrix`: `auto_proceed` states → answer via `SendInput`; `pause_for_human`/`escalate_to_approval` → the run transitions to `needs_review` and hands off via the existing approval workflow. Risky/irreversible prompts (e.g. `RequestHuman` / a destructive-state classification) **always** escalate.

### Ecosystem-fit (reflected here per `ecosystem-fit` / `docs/concepts/ECOSYSTEM.md`)
- **Served interface (agent-manager):** interactive Run becomes a new *programmatic + agentic* capability on `AgentManagerService` — any scenario can ask agent-manager to "drive this interactive CLI to done," not just run a headless prompt.
- **Enabled interface / compound value (`packages/computer-use-agent`):** the loop is now a **reusable enabler**. The first two adapters are browser (BAS) and terminal (web-console). A third surface (desktop GUI, mobile via the Trusted Node Bridge, a remote VM) reuses the same loop by implementing the adapter seam only — this is the compound-intelligence payoff: the system "learns" computer-use once and applies it everywhere.
- **Functional role:** P5 sits at the intersection of Track B (execution) and Track A (accounting) — interactive runs flow into the same UsageEvent spine, so cost/credit accounting is unified across headless and interactive execution.

---
validation_strategy:
**`packages/computer-use-agent` (vitest):**
- Loop unit tests (ported): step progression, max-steps, `done`, abort/resume (`agent.ts:664/675`).
- Loop-detection tests (ported): scroll-ineffective, same-element-click, default-repeat thresholds.
- Action parser tests (ported): all parse formats → `ComputerAction`.
- Seam test: a fake `SurfaceAdapter` + fake `visionClient` drives the loop deterministically to `Done` (proves surface-agnosticism).
- `var`-style compile assertions equivalent: the browser adapter (BAS) and terminal adapter both satisfy `SurfaceAdapter` (typecheck).

**BAS (jest, parity):**
- Existing vision-navigate integration tests pass unchanged (behavior parity is the acceptance bar).
- A test asserts BAS's `BrowserSurfaceAdapter` implements the package `ObserveService`/`ActionExecutor`.
- `grep` guard: zero references to retired loop names in BAS.

**agent-manager (go test):**
- `WebConsoleLauncher` unit test with a fake web-console Connect client: `Launch` creates a session, `Stdout()` yields conversation events, `Kill()` deletes, `Wait()` returns on exit.
- `LauncherSelector.PickFor` routing test: `exec_mode=interactive` → `WebConsoleLauncher`; headless → host/sandbox unchanged (extend `launcher_selector` tests).
- Quiesce test: an interactive run is in `quiesceActiveStatuses`, drains/force-cancels correctly (extend `quiesce_test.go`).
- Recovery test: restart re-attaches an interactive run to its session via `Recover` (adopt-not-kill).
- **Autonomy gate test** (the critical safety test): `auto_proceed` → `SendInput`; `escalate_to_approval`/unknown/destructive → `needs_review` + approval; **a `request_human`/destructive prompt is never auto-answered** (fail-closed). Use a fake `AutonomyGate` driven by a table of P4-shaped states.
- UsageEvent test: an interactive run emits `UsageEvent{kind=agent_run}` into a fake P1 sink with the step token totals.
- Proto parity: `cmd/gen-endpoints --check` / `validateTransport` passes; endpoint-descriptor ↔ RPC parity for the new interactive RPCs.

**Integration / live (Phase 5):** restart all three scenarios; `vrooli scenario test <each>` (block once with `test-genie runs wait --json`); drive a scripted interactive CLI end-to-end through the terminal adapter and confirm a destructive prompt escalates.

---
risks_hazards:
- **R-1 — TS/Go boundary for the terminal adapter (D-3).** A Node sidecar adds operational surface. *Mitigation:* the sidecar is owned by the interactive run (started/stopped with it, supervised like the `LaunchedProcess`); it speaks only web-console Connect-RPC; failure = run failure, recoverable via `Recover`. Reject a Go re-port (drift).
- **R-2 — No web-console server-side event stream.** Conversation events are polled by sequence cursor (`conversation_store.go:365`), not streamed. *Mitigation:* the `WebConsoleLauncher` `Stdout()` reader polls with `WaitIdle`-paced backoff (the same primitive web-console's own WS forwarder uses); this is acceptable for interactive cadence and avoids inventing a new web-console RPC.
- **R-3 — Autonomy gate could auto-answer a destructive prompt.** *Mitigation:* fail-closed default (unknown/destructive → escalate), `request_human` always escalates, and a dedicated safety test (§9) gates it. This is the single highest-severity risk; treat the safety test as a release blocker.
- **R-4 — BAS behavior regression during extraction.** *Mitigation:* Phase 2 acceptance bar is *behavior parity* on BAS's existing vision-navigate tests; baseline diff on BAS must be exit 0 after restart.
- **R-5 — Proto regen drift across three trees.** *Mitigation:* regen in the same phase as the proto change; `validateTransport` + endpoint parity tests; no `make breaking` mid-dev.
- **R-6 — Dual ESM/CJS build complexity (D-6).** *Mitigation:* follow a known dual-build `exports` map; the CJS condition is what `@vrooli/playwright-driver` (esbuild CommonJS) consumes, ESM for the sidecar; vitest covers both via the `exports` resolution.
- **R-7 — P4/P1 contracts not yet merged when P5 executes (cross-plan ordering).** *Mitigation:* the only hard couplings are the `AutonomyGate` (Phase 5.1) and `UsageEvent` sink (Phase 5.2). Both sit behind a thin agent-manager interface with a safe default impl (gate = escalate-everything fail-closed; sink = no-op). Phases 1–4 land with no P4/P1 dependency; Phase 5 swaps in the real impls once P4/P1 merge. State this dependency explicitly to the executor.
- **R-8 — `covdata` toolchain-cache env gotcha** can red the agent-manager UNIT phase ~6-8s with a "go: no such tool covdata" error unrelated to this work (see project memory). *Mitigation:* if seen, apply the documented cache-tool fix; do not attribute it to P5.

This plan is a **greenfield hard cutover**. Non-negotiable:

- **No compatibility layers, no dead code, no re-exports, no `_unused`/`_deprecated` shims, no "v2 alongside v1".** When the computer-use loop moves out of BAS into `packages/computer-use-agent`, the BAS copy is **deleted** in the same phase that lands the import rewrite — BAS imports the package or nothing.
- **Delete stale vocabulary as you go.** Once BAS consumes the package, the words "vision-agent" / "vision-navigate" as *the loop's name* are retired in favor of the package's generic surface (`computer-use-agent`, `surface adapter`, `ObserveService`, `ActionExecutor`). BAS keeps only its **browser surface adapter** vocabulary.
- **No `make breaking` mid-development.** Proto changes regenerate all three trees (Go, TS, descriptor) within the phase that introduces them; the tree is buildable at the end of every phase.
- **Edit files individually.** No mass-rewrite scripts across files.
- The **final phase** is cutover + cleanup + restart of affected scenarios (`agent-manager`, `web-console`, `browser-automation-studio`) + health verify.

preserved_legacy_sections.heading: 7. Implementation Strategy (PHASED)
preserved_legacy_sections.content:
Each phase is independently buildable and verifiable. The tree builds at the end of every phase; proto regen happens in the phase that introduces the proto change. No `make breaking` mid-development.

> Phase ordering rationale: the **package extraction (P1→P2)** is independent of the agent-manager Go work and can land first (lowest cross-plan coupling). The **agent-manager interactive run (P3→P4)** depends only on web-console (already shipped) and the run-domain change. The **autonomy gate (P5)** and **UsageEvent emission** are the only P4/P1-coupled bits and land last.

preserved_legacy_sections.heading: 8. Contract Decisions
preserved_legacy_sections.content:
- **D-1 — `LaunchedProcess` is the Run↔Session boundary.** `WebConsoleLauncher` makes a web-console session *look like a launched process* to agent-manager's runner core. `Stdout()` = conversation-event stream (polled by sequence cursor), `Kill()`/`Signal()` = session delete/close, `Wait()` = session-exited. The Session is referenced **by id only**; there is no parallel lifecycle and no web-console→agent-manager callback. This realizes the LOCKED decision "Session is a detail of the launcher, like a PID."
- **D-2 — New orthogonal Run axes.** `RunKind {coding-agent, llm-call}` and `RunExecMode {headless, interactive}` are **new and orthogonal** to the existing sandbox `RunMode {sandboxed, in_place}`. Do not overload `RunMode`. Default `coding-agent`/`headless` keeps every existing run identical.
- **D-3 — Where the TS loop runs for the terminal adapter.** The package is TypeScript; agent-manager is Go. **Decision:** agent-manager owns a per-interactive-run **Node sidecar** that runs `@vrooli/computer-use-agent` with the terminal `SurfaceAdapter`; the adapter's `observe`/`act` call web-console's Connect-RPC directly (TS Connect-Web client). agent-manager supervises the sidecar as part of the run (it is the "process" the `WebConsoleLauncher` conceptually owns). Rationale: reuse the *exact same* loop as BAS (no Go re-port that would drift); the sidecar is small and disposable. (Rejected: re-port the loop to Go → guarantees drift, violates the single-loop goal.)
- **D-4 — Observe mode is configurable + model-aware.** `OBSERVE_TEXT` (default) feeds `GetScreen.plain_text` to the model; `OBSERVE_SCREENSHOT` renders a screenshot only when the resolved model is a vision model (`model-registry.supportsComputerUse()`). Cheap/non-vision models never pay for a screenshot. Realizes the LOCKED "prefer decoded text ScreenView; screenshot only for vision models."
- **D-5 — Autonomy gate is fail-closed and reuses the existing approval workflow.** `auto_proceed` → `SendInput`; `pause_for_human`/`escalate_to_approval`/unknown/destructive → `needs_review` + existing `ApproveRun`/`RejectRun`. No new approval surface is invented. The gate consumes P4's matrix; it does not define states or detectors.
- **D-6 — Package build is dual-format (ESM + CJS).** `@vrooli/computer-use-agent` is authored ESM (like `iframe-bridge`) but emits both ESM and CJS so the CommonJS `@vrooli/playwright-driver` (esbuild `--platform=node`) and an ESM/Node sidecar both consume it without a wrapper. `exports` map carries `import` + `require` conditions.
- **D-7 — Action vocabulary is preserved, renamed for surface-neutrality.** The 10 verbs (`click`/`type`/`scroll`/`navigate`/`hover`/`select`/`wait`/`keypress`/`done`/`request_human`) are surface-agnostic; the type is renamed `BrowserAction → ComputerAction`. Terminal adapter supports the subset that maps to `SendInput` (`type`, `keypress`, `wait`, `done`, `request_human`); browser-only verbs (`navigate`, `hover`, `select`) are no-ops/errors on the terminal adapter (adapter declares supported verbs).
- **D-8 — Proto: interactive runs are Connect-RPC, no new REST exception.** `kind`/`exec_mode` are added to existing run messages; live-screen access is `GetRunScreen` (unary) or `StreamRunScreen` (server-streaming) per `api-steer` naming. `.vrooli/endpoints.json` regenerated from `Module.Endpoints`; `validateTransport` enforces.
- **D-9 — Dependencies via SDA only.** Every package dependency (`zod`, vision-client SDK, etc.) is installed via `scenario-dependency-analyzer deps install …`, never raw `pnpm add` (Critical Rule §5).
